column15: For in truth there is no void outside of Hashem into which speech travels, the utterance being the initial innovation that expands and concretizes into “and it was so.” Yet for light emerging from darkness, animal soul, and speaking spirit, “and it was so” is not said; for the light was born out of darkness, animal life was a complete radical departure from lifeless matter, and human speech was an entirely transcendent leap.

column13: Full sacrificial atonement (kapparah) is required only for sacred offerings (Kodashim), meaning for entering the innermost Sanctuary and for one striving for transcendent holiness; but for basic ritual purity (tohorah), bodily immersion in a mikveh suffices, representing man's initial awakening from below; while the setting of the sun (he'erev shemesh), which occurs passively without human intervention, represents the final divine assistance granted to one who comes to purify himself.
column15: Yet in the Flood generation all flesh corrupted its way, mixing roots until animals lost awareness of their origin; whereupon all animals consented to be elevated through human eating into the human form, ascending to a higher spiritual plane.

column15: For Chochmah in its own essence possesses immense strength and fortitude, clearly seeing that the Blessed Name directs and brings everything into existence, and that there is nothing whatsoever outside of Him. column15: Nevertheless, because the Dispersion exhibited the outward virtue of unity and mutual love, a remnant survived: they were not blotted out entirely, but merely dispersed — Hashem withdrawing His unifying presence so that their artificial connection dissolved, without obliterating their physical existence.
